doc_title: Introduction to Variables and Data Types
source: CK-12 Computer Science Concepts, Section 4.1, CC-BY-NC
notes: Class B document (14 units). Covers variables, data types (int/float/string/bool), and a worked code trace example. One ECU for the worked example.

units.label: Hook: labeled storage boxes analogy (image)
units.content_summary: Illustration of labeled storage boxes (age, name, isStudent) each containing a value, used as an analogy for variables storing data in memory.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: define a variable; identify the four basic data types; declare and assign variables; trace variable values through a short program.

units.label: Definition: variable (text)
units.content_summary: A variable is a named location in memory that stores a value which can change during program execution. Declared with a name and (in many languages) a type: e.g. `int age = 12;`.

units.label: Data type: integer (text)
units.content_summary: Integer (int): whole numbers, positive or negative, no decimal point. Examples: -5, 0, 42, 1000. Used for counting, indexing, and whole-number arithmetic.

units.label: Data type: float (text)
units.content_summary: Float (floating-point): numbers with a decimal point. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0. Used for measurements, calculations requiring precision beyond whole numbers.

units.label: Data type: string and boolean (text)
units.content_summary: String: sequence of characters in quotes, e.g. "Hello". Boolean: only two values, true or false, used for conditions and logic (e.g. isStudent = true).

units.label: Data types summary table (image)
units.content_summary: Table with four rows (int, float, string, boolean), each showing the type name, an example value, and a typical use case.

units.label: Worked example: variable declarations (text)
units.content_summary: Code snippet: `int age = 12; float price = 4.99; string name = "Amina"; boolean isStudent = true;` Each line explained: type keyword, variable name, assignment operator, value.

units.label: Worked example trace diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Memory-box diagram showing each variable from the worked example with its name, type label, and stored value after execution.

units.label: Naming conventions (text)
units.content_summary: Variable names should be descriptive, start with a letter, contain no spaces, and are case-sensitive. camelCase convention shown (e.g. studentAge, totalPrice).

units.label: Video: variables in action (video)
units.content_summary: Short video showing a simple program running step by step, with variable values displayed and updated live in a debugger-style view as the program executes.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Four problems: identify the correct data type for a list of values; write variable declarations for given scenarios; trace variable values through a short code snippet; find naming convention errors.
